experiment: E9 trained support cardinality and operator scaling
hypothesis: The mass-aware permutation posterior and convex projection retain an Energy advantage over cardinality-matched ASCENT when the source and target supports are trained natively at K=3 and K=7.
rival: The K=5 result is a cardinality-specific effect, or approximation error at K=7 removes the gain.

models.source: native ASCENT signed coupled support and categorical mass
models.target: native positive-speed/pitch support with SPO+ decision costs
models.risk_operator: frozen target backbone plus full-mode expected-ADE risk operator
models.K5_reference: frozen MABPT v1.0.0 checkpoints and results

operators.topM_backend: enumerate then truncate; approximation-quality result only, not a scalable Murty runtime claim
operators.projection: the same fixed MABPT convex Energy-KL projection for every correspondence operator

failure_criteria: exact MABPT Energy fails to improve over cardinality-matched source ASCENT in either fold
K7 exact inference exceeds the declared practical latency budget
top-M approximation error is too large to support a scalability claim
claim_boundary: This is a retrospective train-date cardinality study. It tests native-cardinality behavior but does not convert the historically opened folds into fresh confirmation.
